info.title: Active Directory API - GlobalRS
info.description:
The GlobalRS Active Directory API provides controlled, limited access to certain functions within the  Active Directory domain. 

All API calls are "scoped" to the account's OU

post.description:
Creates an OU for the account number and initializes the OU with standard objects and permissions.

The following actions are performed
  - Create the Account OU
  - Remove default permissions for EVERYONE and AUTHENTICATED_USERS
  - Create **Customer Objects** sub-OU
  - Create **<_account_>-AllUsers** group
  - Create **<_account_>-Admins** group
  - Create **<_account_>-Rax** group
  - Create **<_account_>-Clusters** group
  - Add **<_account_>-Admins** to the **<_account_>-AllUsers** group
  - Add **<_account_>-Rax** to the **<_account_>-AllUsers** group
  - Add **<_account_>-Clusters** to the **<_account_>-AllUsers** group
  - Grant READ on account OU to **<_account_>-AllUsers**
  - Grant CREATE COMPUTER on account OU to **<_account_>-Clusters**
  - Grant READ/WRITE _ServicePrincipalName_ property on account OU to **<_account_>-Clusters**

get.description:
Returns an **adContainer** object for the OU and all its descendant objects and containers/OUs.

The _path_ querystring parameter can be used to indicate the _root_ of the search, i.e., where in the OU structure the search should begin.  If the _path_ querystring parameter is present, it must be a DN to an existing OU(within the account OU structure).  Only objects in this OU and its descendants will be returned.  If _path_ is not provided, the account OU will be used as the search root.

post.summary: Create OU within an account OU
post.description:
Creates a new OU within the account OU structure. 

If the _path_ querystring parameter is present, it must be a DN to an existing OU(within the account OU structure) that will be the _parent_ of the new OU, otherwise the new OU will be created within the account OU itself.

schema.description: name of the new OU to create, in quotes

get.description:
Returns an **apiCollection** of resource URL's that match the given criteria.

The _path_ querystring parameter can be used to indicate the _root_ of the search, i.e., where in the OU structure the search should begin.  If the _path_ querystring parameter is present, it must be a DN to an existing OU(within the account OU structure).  Only computers in this OU and its descendants will be returned.  If _path_ is not provided, the account OU will be used as the search root.

The _filter_ querystring parameter can be used to limit the results to computers that match specific LDAP attributes.   if _filter_ is empty or missing, then ALL computers in the search root(and descendant OUs) will be returned.

post.description:
Creates a new computer account.  If the computer object already exists in the Computers container, the object will be moved into the account OU.  Otherwise, the object will be created directly in the OU.

If the CORE device number passed in to the API is a cluster device, then the API will create **ALL** computer objects associated with the cluster, including other cluster devices, such as the NTClus, MSDTC, etc, as well as the physical nodes the cluster is running on. 


Note that the newly created account is automatically added to the **<_account_>-AllUsers** group, unless it is a cluster, in which case each cluster object is added to the **<_account_>-Clusters** group.

This API can be called multiple times to create any missing cluster-related computer object(s)

delete.description: Deletes a computer object from the account OU

get.description: Returns an **apiCollection** of users URL's that match the given criteria.

post.description: Create a user account.  Note that the newly created account is automatically added to the **<_account_>-AllUsers** group

Creates SQL Server service accounts to run various SQL services. All service accounts created will end with a numerical sequence number, which is associated with a particular SQL Server instance.

The following actions are performed
  - Create **<_account_>-SQLSVC#** service account
  - Create **<_account_>-AGTSVC#** service account
  - [_Optional_] Create **<_account_>-RPTSVC#** service account
  - [_Optional_] Create **<_account_>-ANLVC#** service account
  - [_Optional_] Create **<_account_>-INTSVC#** service account
  - Create **<_account_>-SvcGroup#** group
  - Add all service accounts created to the **<_account_>-SvcGroup#** group
  - Add ***<_account_>-SvcGroup#** to the **<_account_>-AllUsers** group
  - Grant READ on **<_account_>-AllUsers** group to **<_account_>-SvcGroup#**
  - Grant FULLCONTROL on **<_account_>-SvcGroup#** to **<_account_>-SQLSVC#** service account
  
The # in the above list refers to a unique sequence number.  The highest numbered **<_account_>-SQLSVC#** that currently exists in the Account OU determines what the next sequence number will be when this API is called to create new service accounts.

if the **sequenceNumber** query parameter is given, the Service Accounts will be generated with that sequence number, instead of calculating the next sequence from the highest numbered **<_account_>-SQLSVC#** that currently exists.  Setting the **sequenceNumber**, will allow the API to be run(or re-run) multiple times to create any missing or new service accounts.

As an example, suppose a customer builds a SQL cluster with just the DB Engine; no Reporting, Analysis, or Integtration Services.  The API will be called with the following data

    POST /domains/globalrs/accounts/{account}/sqlserviceaccounts
      {
          "instanceName": "MSSQL",
          "createBackupAccount": false,
          "reportingServices": false,
          "analysisServices": false,
          "integrationServices": false
      }
  which will create the SQLSVC1 and AGTSVC1 service accounts and place them into the SvcGroup1 group.  Later the custer decides to add Reporting and Analysis Services to their SQL instance. The API can be called again with the **sequenceNumber** set to 1
  
    POST /domains/globalrs/accounts/{account}/sqlserviceaccounts?sequenceNumber=1
      {
          "instanceName": "MSSQL",
          "createBackupAccount": false,
          "reportingServices": true,  <==== NOTE
          "analysisServices": true,   <==== NOTE
          "integrationServices": false
      }
      
  The API will then create the RPTSVC1 and ANLSVC1 service accounts and place them into the SvcGroup1 group

get.description:
Returns an AdUser object with data about the given user.  

Note that if you specify any attributes to retrieve, the value in each attribute is presented as it exists in AD; the value is not parsed, translated nor formatted.

For example, the **accountexpires** attributes is presented as a very large number, like 132010588092732488.  This is actually Microsoft's FILETIME format(see *https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/desktop/api/minwinbase/ns-minwinbase-filetime*).

put.description: Adds an object to a group.

delete.description: Deletes a user object from the account OU

get.description: Returns an **apiCollection** of resource URL's that match the given criteria.

post.description: Creates a new AD group in the Account OU.  Only Security Groups can be created via this API -- Distribution Groups are not supported.

delete.description: Deletes a group object from the account OU

get.description:
Returns an **apiCollection** of resource URL's that match the given criteria. 

Since Active Directory only stores the Distinguished Name(DN) of each member, the only way to determine if the member is a user, computer, or another group, is to retrieve that object using the DN. For very large groups, this means extremely long execution times.  

For that reason, this API returns the member DN in the form of links to the  **/domains/{domainName}/objects/{PathDN}** API endpoint.  It is left to the caller to determine if the objects API should be called to collect more data on the member.

post.description: Adds an object to a group.

schema.description:
The DistinguishedName(DN) of the object to be added to the group.
Note that the DN must be enclosed in quotes, either single(') or double(") will work

delete.description: Removes an object from a group

get.description: Returns an **apiCollection** of resource URL's that match the given criteria.

dn.description: the DistinguishedName of the AD Object(User, Group, OU, etc).

name.description: the internal name of the AD object

displayName.description: the display name for the AD object

classList.description: a list of AD classes this object is based on

domainName.description: the netBIOS domain name that this object is a member of

attributes.description: a dictionary (or associative array) of LDAP attribute names and their corresponding values.

isContainer.description: indicates where this object is a container or an OU, which may contain other objects

isUser.description: indicates where this object is a user object

isGroup.description: indicates where this object is a group object

isComputer.description: indicates where this object is a computer object

isForeignSecurityPrincipal.description: indicates whether this object is a foreign security principal that exists in another domain or forest

sites.description:
an array of valid site names within the domain.
A site name can be used on some endpoints to force a change to occur in that site before replicating out to other sites

userid.description: the unique userid of the user; comes from the LDAP *sAMAccountName* attribute

firstName.description: the user's first name(given name); comes from the LDAP *givenName* attribute

lastName.description: the user's last name(surname); comes from the LDAP *sn* attribute

enabled.description: indicates if the account is enabled or not

lockedOut.description: TRUE if the account is locked out; Note that the **LockedOut** property cannot be programtically set to TRUE; it can only be set to FALSE to unlock the account

userid.description: the unique userid of the user

firstName.description: the user's first name(given name). Can be blank/empty if **fullName** is provided

lastName.description: the user's last name(surname).  Can be blank/empty if **fullName** is provided

fullName.description: if empty, this will be automatically populated by concatenating the **firstName** and **lastName**

enabled.description: indicates if the user should should be enabled or not when it is created.

serviceAccount.description:
Indicates if the new user account is a service account.

Note that service account generally have a non-expiring password

adNewSQLServiceAccounts.description: Parameters to indicate what SQL Server service accounts to create for a particular SQL Server instance

instanceName.description: The name of the MS SQL Server Instance

createBackupAccount.description: if **true**, a service account for performing backups will be created

reportingServices.description: if **true**, a service account will be created for running SQL Reporting Services

analysisServices.description: if **true**, a service account will be created for running SQL Analysis Services

integrationServices.description: if **true**, a service account will be created for running SQL Integration Services

isScurityGroup.description: Indicates if this is a security group or not

name.description: the unique internal name of the group

groupScope.description: The security scope of the new group

enabled.description: Indicates if this is a computer object is enabled or not

isScurityGroup.description: Indicates if this is a security group or not

childObjects.description: a recursive array of all object within the OU

userid.name: userid
userid.description: either the sAMAccount name or the DistinguishedName(DN) of the user to retrieve

groupid.name: groupid
groupid.description: either the sAMAccount name or the DistinguishedName(DN) of the group

Site.name: site
Site.description: AD Site name.  When making a change the API will connect to a Domain Controller in this site to make the change.  The AD replication topology will replicate the change(s) from there.

OUPath.name: path
OUPath.description: the DistinguishedName(DN) of the container or OU to be used as the root level for the operation. For GET operations, only the container at <_path_> and its child containers will be searched for matching. objects.  For POST operation, the new object will be created in the container specified by <_path_>.

OUPathRequired.name: path
OUPathRequired.description: the DistinguishedName(DN) of the container or OU to be used as the root level of the search.  Only the container and its child containers will be searched for matching objects

DN.name: dn
DN.description: the DistinguishedName(DN) of the object to retrieve

LDAPFilter.name: filter
LDAPFilter.description:
a valid LDAP filter.  Only objects that match the given filter will be returned.  if not present, links to all objects of the given type(users, gorups, etc) will be returned.

Refer to https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa996205%28v=exchg.65%29.aspx?f=255&MSPPError=-2147217396 for help writing LDAP filters

LDAPAttributes.name: attributes
LDAPAttributes.description:
[OPTIONAL] a comma-separated list(with no spaces) of valid LDAP attribute names.

The values for each attribute will be returned in the "attributes" property of the returned object.  if the attribute name does not exist or has no value, its "attribute" property in the returned object will be set to NULL

deviceName.name: name
deviceName.description: computer name, CORE device number, or DN of a computer object

svcAcctSeqNumber.name: sequenceNumber
svcAcctSeqNumber.description: the sequence number to use when generating SQL Service account(s)

201.description: The requested AD object was created. a link to the newly created object is returned in the headers

204.description: The request was successful, but no data is returned

400.description: There was something wrong with the input data either in the body of the request or in the querystring portion of the URL.  The specific error will be returned in the body of the HTTp Response.

403.description:
- You do not have the necessary permission(s) to perform this action
- the Identity token was not provided in the Header
- the Identity token provided in the header has expired

404.description:
The item you are looking for was not found.

This could be any of the following
  - the domain specified in the URL was not found
  - the account specified in the URL was not found
  - the AD object(user, group, computer, etc) specified in the URL was not found

authTokenRequired.name: X-Auth-Token
authTokenRequired.description: a valid Identity token must be provided in the header of the request
